allowed_claims: Loops can send Supabase Auth emails through Supabase Auth’s Send Email Hook using a Supabase Edge Function and one Loops template per auth email type.

assets.title: Supabase’s Send Email Hook still needs an Edge Function
assets.content:
Subject: Supabase’s Send Email Hook still needs an Edge Function
Preview text: Each configured auth action also needs its own Loops template and a verified sending domain.

Route Supabase Auth email through Loops

Hi there,

Supabase’s built-in sender is a test-only, rate-limited path. Moving auth email off it still leaves a replacement route to implement.

Loops is an email sending platform for SaaS that can handle Supabase Auth email through the Send Email Hook. Supabase calls an Edge Function you deploy; that function verifies the request and sends the matching Loops transactional email.

Each configured auth action type needs its own Loops template. A verified Loops sending domain is also required before those messages can send.

The Supabase documentation lays out this architecture and its required components, so you can judge whether the hook, Edge Function, action-specific templates, and verified domain fit your Auth setup before implementing it.

Read the Supabase docs → https://loops.so/docs/integrations/supabase

- Loops

selected_brief.target_audience: A Supabase or Clerk app team moving auth and onboarding email off the platform's built-in defaults before launch
selected_brief.job: Get the reader to assess whether the documented Send Email Hook architecture and prerequisites fit its Supabase Auth setup.
selected_brief.single_idea: Loops provides a documented Send Email Hook route for sending Supabase Auth email through an Edge Function and action-specific Loops templates.
selected_brief.felt_need: The built-in platform sender's per-project hourly email cap stops signup, confirmation, recovery and invite mail once more than a trickle of users (or of their own test attempts) arrive, surfacing as HTTP 429 / 'email rate limit exceeded' on the signup path.
selected_brief.mechanism: The documented route uses Supabase's Send Email Hook, a Supabase Edge Function, and one Loops transactional template per configured auth action type. Sending also requires a verified Loops sending domain.
selected_brief.belief_shift: Before: Loops is a familiar email platform, but its role in Supabase Auth is abstract. After: the reader understands the specific hook, Edge Function, template, and domain requirements well enough to judge architectural fit.
must_not_say: Do not claim that Loops removes, raises, bypasses, or otherwise changes Supabase's own auth-email rate limit or resolves HTTP 429 errors.
Do not claim that the reader has already encountered failed signups, missing emails, rate-limit errors, or a failed migration.
Do not claim that upgrading a Supabase plan changes or does not change its built-in sender limit.
Do not imply that this authentication-email proposition applies to Clerk; Clerk continues to send its own authentication emails.
Do not claim instant, effortless, no-code, or measured setup time.
Do not promise deliverability, inbox placement, launch readiness, reliability, or business results.
Do not introduce onboarding workflows, pricing, the Free plan, customer results, or the broader integration catalogue; this email owns the Auth Hook mechanism.
Do not say every possible Auth email will go through Loops without the required matching configuration.
Do not invent urgency, discounts, prior visits, conversations, or deadlines.

Keep the connection route attached to its cited source. A native or prebuilt integration and a custom HTTP/webhook endpoint are separate setup paths unless the source explicitly equates them. A platform name alone establishes neither manual endpoint configuration nor a no-setup connector. Keep unknown setup requirements unknown; do not mix the steps or benefits of those paths.
Restrict this campaign to Supabase.
A Loops sending domain must be added and verified before auth email will send (E42).
The SPF, DKIM, MX and DMARC records Loops supplies must be copied into DNS; Loops recommends a sending subdomain such as mail.yourcompany.com (E251, E261).
The Send Email Hook route requires a Supabase Edge Function and one Loops template per auth action type (E1).
The SMTP route requires at least the Confirm signup and Magic Link templates, with Confirm signup's variables also present in Magic Link (E395, E387).
The post-signup onboarding sequence requires the separate Supabase contact-sync setup; the Send Email Hook covers auth email only (E37, E380).

The Clerk branch is only partly served: Loops syncs Clerk users and can run onboarding workflows (E274, E276), but Clerk keeps sending its own authentication emails (E285), so a Clerk team cannot move auth email itself to Loops. On the Supabase branch, SMTP covers five auth types only (E225, E387), an auth type without a Loops template falls back to Supabase's own sender (E230), and unmapped action types are silently skipped in the documented Edge Function (E41). Regional sending, which the audience definition already marks unverified, is not established by the selected evidence, and nothing in the selected evidence speaks to Supabase's own auth-email rate limit.

Loops becomes the sender for these auth email types, but the selected evidence establishes nothing about the auth platform's own auth-email rate limit, which P3 reports continues to apply; on the SMTP route only five types are covered (E225, E387) and an untemplated type falls back to Supabase's own sender (E230).

The documented material names Loops-side prerequisites and failure modes (required templates, verified domain, fallback to Supabase's sender, silently skipped unmapped action types) but establishes nothing about the reported 500 and 535 errors inside Supabase's own SMTP configuration or about recovering after reverting; the report is single-source and undat…

Selected audience: A Supabase or Clerk app team moving auth and onboarding email off the platform's built-in defaults before launch.
Research context describes some members of this market, not this recipient's installed tools or experiences. Follow the campaign request when it scopes the job.
Observed situation (grounded; check applicability): Small software teams running Supabase Auth in a real app reach a point — beta registration, App Store submission, opening public signup — where the platform's built-in email sender stops being adequate and auth mail (signup confirmation, recovery, invites, magic links) must be moved onto their own SMTP provider or Send Email hook on a verified domain. brief.reader_segment: A Supabase or Clerk app team moving auth and onboarding email off the platform's built-in defaults before launch
brief.promise: A Supabase team can evaluate a documented route for sending Auth email through Loops, with the architecture and prerequisites stated plainly before it commits.
brief.orientation: Loops is an email sending platform that can handle Supabase Auth email through Supabase's Send Email Hook.
brief.arc: In one email, move the reader from general awareness of Loops to understanding one concrete Supabase Auth mechanism and inspecting its documented setup.
brief.sequence_rationale: A single consideration email should make one checkable argument rather than recap the platform. The Send Email Hook mechanism directly matches the qualified Supabase audience's task, while the documentation is a proportionate read-only next step for a prospect. The email must disclose the Edge Function, per-action templates, and verified-domain requirement, and it must not imply that changing the sender alters Supabase's own auth-email rate limit.

emails.selection_reason: This audience is already solution-aware and evaluating an authentication-email send path. The documented Send Email Hook architecture gives it a concrete fit question to answer without requiring registration or deployment first.

value_case.reader_benefit: If the team wants Loops to handle its Supabase Auth email, it can give each configured auth action its own Loops transactional template while Supabase invokes the send path through a hook.
value_case.mechanism: Supabase's Send Email Hook calls a Supabase Edge Function, which sends the corresponding Loops transactional email; the setup uses one Loops template for each configured auth action type.
decision_conditions: A verified Loops sending domain is required.
The Send Email Hook route requires a Supabase Edge Function and a Loops template for each configured auth action type.

emails.target_audience: A Supabase or Clerk app team moving auth and onboarding email off the platform's built-in defaults before launch
emails.job: Get the reader to assess whether the documented Send Email Hook architecture and prerequisites fit its Supabase Auth setup.
emails.single_idea: Loops provides a documented Send Email Hook route for sending Supabase Auth email through an Edge Function and action-specific Loops templates.
emails.felt_need: The built-in platform sender's per-project hourly email cap stops signup, confirmation, recovery and invite mail once more than a trickle of users (or of their own test attempts) arrive, surfacing as HTTP 429 / 'email rate limit exceeded' on the signup path.
emails.mechanism: The documented route uses Supabase's Send Email Hook, a Supabase Edge Function, and one Loops transactional template per configured auth action type. Sending also requires a verified Loops sending domain.
emails.belief_shift: Before: Loops is a familiar email platform, but its role in Supabase Auth is abstract. After: the reader understands the specific hook, Edge Function, template, and domain requirements well enough to judge architectural fit.
must_not_say: Do not claim that Loops removes, raises, bypasses, or otherwise changes Supabase's own auth-email rate limit or resolves HTTP 429 errors.
Do not claim that the reader has already encountered failed signups, missing emails, rate-limit errors, or a failed migration.
Do not claim that upgrading a Supabase plan changes or does not change its built-in sender limit.
Do not imply that this authentication-email proposition applies to Clerk; Clerk continues to send its own authentication emails.
Do not claim instant, effortless, no-code, or measured setup time.
Do not promise deliverability, inbox placement, launch readiness, reliability, or business results.
Do not introduce onboarding workflows, pricing, the Free plan, customer results, or the broader integration catalogue; this email owns the Auth Hook mechanism.
Do not say every possible Auth email will go through Loops without the required matching configuration.
Do not invent urgency, discounts, prior visits, conversations, or deadlines.

Keep the connection route attached to its cited source. A native or prebuilt integration and a custom HTTP/webhook endpoint are separate setup paths unless the source explicitly equates them. A platform name alone establishes neither manual endpoint configuration nor a no-setup connector. Keep unknown setup requirements unknown; do not mix the steps or benefits of those paths.
Restrict this campaign to Supabase.
A Loops sending domain must be added and verified before auth email will send (E42).
The SPF, DKIM, MX and DMARC records Loops supplies must be copied into DNS; Loops recommends a sending subdomain such as mail.yourcompany.com (E251, E261).
The Send Email Hook route requires a Supabase Edge Function and one Loops template per auth action type (E1).
The SMTP route requires at least the Confirm signup and Magic Link templates, with Confirm signup's variables also present in Magic Link (E395, E387).
The post-signup onboarding sequence requires the separate Supabase contact-sync setup; the Send Email Hook covers auth email only (E37, E380).

The Clerk branch is only partly served: Loops syncs Clerk users and can run onboarding workflows (E274, E276), but Clerk keeps sending its own authentication emails (E285), so a Clerk team cannot move auth email itself to Loops. On the Supabase branch, SMTP covers five auth types only (E225, E387), an auth type without a Loops template falls back to Supabase's own sender (E230), and unmapped action types are silently skipped in the documented Edge Function (E41). Regional sending, which the audience definition already marks unverified, is not established by the selected evidence, and nothing in the selected evidence speaks to Supabase's own auth-email rate limit.

Loops becomes the sender for these auth email types, but the selected evidence establishes nothing about the auth platform's own auth-email rate limit, which P3 reports continues to apply; on the SMTP route only five types are covered (E225, E387) and an untemplated type falls back to Supabase's own sender (E230).

The documented material names Loops-side prerequisites and failure modes (required templates, verified domain, fallback to Supabase's sender, silently skipped unmapped action types) but establishes nothing about the reported 500 and 535 errors inside Supabase's own SMTP configuration or about recovering after reverting; the report is single-source and undat…
emails.objection: The team may reasonably want to know what the integration requires before committing to another sending path.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether a Send Email Hook using a Supabase Edge Function, action-specific Loops templates, and a verified sending domain fits the team's Auth email architecture.
emails.next_step_value: The documentation lays out Loops' Supabase integration and the documented Auth email route so the reader can inspect the required components before setting it up.
emails.next_step_limit: Reading the documentation does not verify production behavior, complete a migration, or establish what happens to Supabase's own auth-email rate limit.
emails.subject_strategy: Name the concrete Supabase Auth mechanism or setup choice; avoid generic product language, outcome promises, and manufactured urgency.

brief.voice_notes: Use Loops' direct, practical register. Lead with the useful operation, keep the technical sequence concrete, and avoid hype or competitive claims.

intelligence.selected_audience: A Supabase or Clerk app team moving auth and onboarding email off the platform's built-in defaults before launch
partial_caveats_injected: A Loops sending domain must be added and verified before auth email will send (E42).
The SPF, DKIM, MX and DMARC records Loops supplies must be copied into DNS; Loops recommends a sending subdomain such as mail.yourcompany.com (E251, E261).
The Send Email Hook route requires a Supabase Edge Function and one Loops template per auth action type (E1).
The SMTP route requires at least the Confirm signup and Magic Link templates, with Confirm signup's variables also present in Magic Link (E395, E387).
The post-signup onboarding sequence requires the separate Supabase contact-sync setup; the Send Email Hook covers auth email only (E37, E380).

The Clerk branch is only partly served: Loops syncs Clerk users and can run onboarding workflows (E274, E276), but Clerk keeps sending its own authentication emails (E285), so a Clerk team cannot move auth email itself to Loops. On the Supabase branch, SMTP covers five auth types only (E225, E387), an auth type without a Loops template falls back to Supabase's own sender (E230), and unmapped action types are silently skipped in the documented Edge Function (E41). Regional sending, which the audience definition already marks unverified, is not established by the selected evidence, and nothing in the selected evidence speaks to Supabase's own auth-email rate limit.

Loops becomes the sender for these auth email types, but the selected evidence establishes nothing about the auth platform's own auth-email rate limit, which P3 reports continues to apply; on the SMTP route only five types are covered (E225, E387) and an untemplated type falls back to Supabase's own sender (E230).
